gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-open-sans: Structural and striking, Stencilia has gaps left open at its curve ends. Open Sans follows in a smooth, modern voice, its bulky lowercase giving the heading a friendly, solid neighbor.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-oxygen: Oxygen reads clean and contemporary, its curves staying open and its lowercase nearly as large as the capitals. Stencilia above it adds the striking part; make that heading the smaller of the two if it feels loud.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-parkinsans: Modern and crisp, Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness throughout, its wide-mouthed letters holding up even when shrunk. And Stencilia up top is the opposite, structural and striking, with a pipe-cleaner feel in every letterform.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-pathway-extreme: Pathway Extreme reads modern and clean, with clear openings in its rounded letters and stubby ascenders beside a large x-height. Its quiet clarity is what lets the structural, striking Stencilia stand out above it.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-prompt: Stencilia brings a structural, striking display look, while Prompt below it is approachable, with oversized small letters and open apertures. The heading makes the statement and the sans-serif text simply carries it.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-pt-sans-caption: Stencilia looks cut and constructed. PT Sans Caption underneath has unclosed, inviting bowls and big-bodied lowercase, so a long passage in it should feel professional, open and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-questrial: Flat, stencil-cut and striking, Stencilia is built on gaps at the ends of its curves, against Questrial's wire-like monoline skeleton. Make the heading small and it loses its punch; make Questrial large and it turns fussy.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big reads neutral and contemporary, its terminals finishing well clear of the stem and its lowercase filling the line. A long passage in this plain sans should feel smooth beneath the wire-cut Stencilia.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-readex-pro: Structural from the first glance, Stencilia sets a bold stage. Readex Pro takes over with broad terminal gaps and horizontals as heavy as its verticals, so the text feels steady beneath the heading's sharp edges.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-ruda: Ruda reads approachable and clean, its wide-mouthed rounds and wire-like monoline skeleton drawn for screens. A long passage in this plain sans moves along smoothly under Stencilia's spaghetti-like display lines.
